assertions.title: SAFETY comments present on UnsafeCell allocations

steps.expected: SAFETY comments adjacent to each unsafe block dereferencing UnsafeCell
steps.observed: Two SAFETY comments found at lines 201 and 317, each preceding an unsafe block that dereferences UnsafeCell socket buffers via .get() + &mut *

steps.action: Verify all unsafe blocks in mqtt_client.rs relate to UnsafeCell
steps.expected: Every unsafe block has a SAFETY comment
steps.observed: Two unsafe blocks (lines 208, 322) both have preceding SAFETY comments explaining the single-task ownership invariant and TcpSocket lifecycle

assertions.evidence: Line 201: 'SAFETY: This is the first and only borrow of these newly-allocated buffers...' before line 208 unsafe block. Line 317: 'SAFETY: The old TcpSocket was dropped above via self.transport.take()...' before line 322 unsafe block. Both explain the single-task mqtt_task ownership invariant.

assertions.title: No raw pointer casts on socket buffers

steps.expected: No matches for raw pointer casts on socket buffer fields
steps.observed: No matches found. Socket buffer reborrow uses UnsafeCell::get() + &mut * pattern exclusively (lines 208, 322)

assertions.evidence: No 'as *mut' or 'as *const' patterns found in mqtt_client.rs. The unsafe dereferences use the pattern: unsafe { &mut *socket_rx_buf.get() } and unsafe { &mut *self.socket_rx_buf.get() }

assertions.title: Sniffer mode uses pre-allocated hex buffer

steps.expected: No per-byte format!() allocation in sniffer loop
steps.observed: format_args!("{:02X}", b) is used inside bytes_to_hex() but routed through core::fmt::write() into a fixed-size HexBuf — no heap allocation. The old pattern .collect() is mentioned only in a comment as what was replaced.

steps.action: Verify no .collect() pattern in sniffer code
steps.observed: No .collect() calls found in sniffer code. The .collect() reference at line 450 is only in a doc comment describing the old pattern.

assertions.evidence: bytes_to_hex() at line 453 uses core::fmt::write(buf, format_args!("{:02X}", b)) into a pre-allocated HexBuf. No alloc::format!().collect() pattern exists in the sniffer code path.

assertions.title: Sniffer hex output correctness

steps.action: Search for hex output tests in workspace
steps.expected: Test verifying hex output for edge cases (0x00, 0x7E, 0x7D, 0xFF)
steps.observed: No hex output unit tests found. The app/ crate is a no_std ESP32 binary with no #[test] or #[cfg(test)] modules. No workspace crate tests for bytes_to_hex.

assertions.evidence: No unit tests exist for bytes_to_hex(). The app/ crate compiles only for xtensa-esp32-none-elf target and has no test infrastructure. Cannot run cargo test for this assertion.
assertions.issues: No automated tests for hex output correctness. The code logic is straightforward (format_args!("{:02X}", b) for each byte) and would produce correct output by virtue of core::fmt::UpperHex, but no explicit test covers edge cases 0x00, 0x7E, 0x7D, 0xFF.

assertions.title: Sniffer buffer size bounded at compile time

steps.observed: HexBuf struct contains data: [u8; 512] (HEX_BUF_SIZE = 512) and len: usize — a fixed-size stack array.

steps.expected: Overflow handled by truncation, not panic
steps.observed: bytes_to_hex() checks buf.remaining() < 2 and breaks (truncates) rather than overflowing. write_str() returns Err(core::fmt::Error) if bytes exceed remaining capacity.

assertions.evidence: HexBuf at line 409: data: [u8; 512], len: usize. HEX_BUF_SIZE = 512 (line 404). Overflow handling: line 457 'if buf.remaining() < 2 { break; }' — truncation, not panic.

assertions.title: MQTT rate limiter drops excess commands

steps.expected: Returns false when count exceeds RATE_LIMIT_MAX_COMMANDS
steps.observed: RateLimiter::check() increments count and returns self.count <= RATE_LIMIT_MAX_COMMANDS. When count > 10, returns false.
check_rate_limit() (line 707) calls warn!() with 'MQTT command rate limited: exceeded {RATE_LIMIT_MAX_COMMANDS} commands per {RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECS}s window' when check() returns false.

steps.expected: RATE_LIMIT_MAX_COMMANDS and RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECS defined as named constants

assertions.evidence: RateLimiter struct with named constants at lines 34-38. check() at line 61 returns false when count > 10. check_rate_limit() at line 707 logs warn!() on drop. Drop logic: commands exceeding 10 per 10-second window are rejected.

assertions.title: Commands under rate limit are not dropped

steps.expected: Returns true (unconditional forward) when count <= RATE_LIMIT_MAX_COMMANDS
steps.observed: check() increments count first, then returns self.count <= RATE_LIMIT_MAX_COMMANDS. For counts 1 through 10, returns true. Count 11+ returns false.

steps.action: Review check_rate_limit() call site in mqtt_task
steps.expected: Commands forwarded when check_rate_limit() returns true
steps.observed: In main.rs mqtt_task, line with 'if mqtt.check_rate_limit() { ... cmd_sender.send(cmd).await; }' — commands are forwarded unconditionally when under limit.

assertions.evidence: RateLimiter::check() returns true for counts 1-10. The check_rate_limit() wrapper returns true directly (no modification). In main.rs, the command is forwarded via cmd_sender.send(cmd).await when check returns true.

assertions.title: Rate window resets correctly

steps.action: Review window expiry logic in RateLimiter::check()
steps.expected: After 10-second window expires, count resets to zero
steps.observed: Lines 64-68: 'if now.duration_since(self.window_start) >= window_duration { self.count = 0; self.window_start = now; }'. Count resets to 0 and window_start is updated to current time.

assertions.evidence: RateLimiter::check() at line 61: window_duration = Duration::from_secs(RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECS). Line 67: self.count = 0 when window expires. Window restarts from current instant.

assertions.title: Only http:// URLs accepted for OTA

steps.expected: URL validation requires http:// prefix, rejects other schemes
steps.observed: Three rejection paths: (1) scheme via :// separator checked != 'http' → None, (2) bare colon (e.g. data:...) checked → None, (3) no scheme at all → None. All non-http schemes are rejected.

assertions.evidence: parse_ota_url() at lines 743-771: Checks url.find('://') for scheme, compares scheme != 'http' → reject. Falls through to check bare ':' for schemes like 'data:'. Falls through to reject no-scheme URLs. Only 'http' scheme passes all checks.

assertions.title: Valid http:// URLs accepted for OTA

steps.expected: http:// URLs with host, port, path are accepted
steps.observed: When scheme is 'http', the function returns Some(String::from(url)) at line 772. The URL is extracted as the raw string between quotes, so any http://host:port/path format passes.

assertions.evidence: parse_ota_url() extracts URL string between quotes, validates scheme is 'http', then returns Some(String::from(url)) at line 772. Standard http:// URLs with IP, port, and path components are accepted.

assertions.title: OTA URL rejection logged

steps.action: Review warn!() calls in rejection paths of parse_ota_url()
steps.expected: warn!() call with scheme in each rejection path
steps.observed: Three warn!() calls: (1) line 752: warn!("OTA URL rejected: unsupported scheme '{}' ...", scheme), (2) line 762: warn!("OTA URL rejected: unsupported scheme '{}' ...", scheme), (3) line 769: warn!("OTA URL rejected: no scheme ...")

assertions.evidence: All three rejection paths include warn!() with the scheme name: line 752 for http-scheme URLs (e.g. https://, ftp://), line 762 for bare-colon schemes (e.g. data:), line 769 for no scheme at all.
